conventions.convention: Ordinary fusion categories are defined over an arbitrary field k. Simple endomorphism algebras Dℓ need not equal k: fusion multiplicities are ranks over Dℓ, and fusion-channel tensor products are balanced over the intermediate simple endomorphism algebra.

The associator points from (X⊗Y)⊗Z to X⊗(Y⊗Z). On outgoing fusion spaces its induced map sends h to h composed with the inverse associator. Left and right duals have the separately displayed evaluation, coevaluation, and snake orientations; unitors are suppressed in those composites.
Tensor invertibility requires one object E with both D⊗E≅1 and E⊗D≅1. Simplicity and tensor invertibility are separate properties.

The fusion 2-category convention assumes an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, finite semisimple Hom categories, adjoints for all 1-morphisms, additive object structure, separable-monad splittings, finitely many simple-object equivalence classes, a Gray-monoid tensor structure, object duals, and a simple tensor unit. Neither unitarity nor physical realization follows from these data.

For the twisted example, G={0,1} has addition modulo 2 and ω(a,b,c)=(-1)^(abc). For the grade-1 simple object, both evaluations have scalar -1 and both coevaluations have scalar 1. The comparison with the untwisted datum concerns specified associator components, without asserting monoidal inequivalence.

load_bearing.statement: A tensor-invertible object D is an object for which some object E satisfies D⊗E≅1 and E⊗D≅1. An object with no such two-sided inverse is non-invertible. The fusion datum includes the actual associator, unitors, and both duality structures, not just the integers N.

For the displayed two-dimensional complex representation V of S3, V⊗V≅1⊕ε⊕V. Rep_C(S3) is a finite semisimple fusion category, V is simple, and V has no tensor inverse. No QFT defect realization is asserted.

The displayed normalized cocycle ω(a,b,c)=(-1)^(abc), associator, and duality data give a finite semisimple fusion category with δa⊗δb≅δ(a+b). Its grade-1 associator component is -id, whereas the untwisted datum has +id with the same fusion multiplicities.
In Vec_Z2, D=δ0⊕δ1 satisfies D⊗D≅2δ0⊕2δ1 and is non-invertible although both simple summands are tensor-invertible. D is reducible, and no physical realization is asserted.

concerns.concern: The Gray-monoid paragraph says the interchanger 'is compatible with composition in each 1-morphism variable, and is compatible with tensoring by an object in either variable', but gives no equations or exact numbered axiom incorporation. Douglas–Reutter, Definition 2.1.1, C4–C6, explicitly specifies these equations, including the middle compatibility φ_(f⊗B,h)=φ_(f,B⊗h). I checked that source at https://arxiv.org/pdf/1812.11933, printed pp. 35–36. The intended standard convention is recoverable, but this portion is less explicit than the task's definition requirement; state the equations or incorporate those exact axioms unambiguously.

seams_checked.note: The page declares the prerequisite, but its two definitions do not invoke the fusion-category item as a logical supplier. Their model-defined correlators, isotopy condition, and conditional interface fusion limit do not infer physical defects from abstract categorical data.

The Ising data definition specifies a candidate; its separate coherence lemma supplies the category axioms and additional unitary structure. The realization theorem's F2 faithfully retains two-sided invertibility and the need for junction and associator data beyond multiplicities. Its physical conclusions are confined to the specified finite lattice model.

The abstract Ising example uses the supplier's two-sided inverse criterion and rules out every right inverse by conflicting simple multiplicities. The three-site example separately invokes the finite-model realization theorem; neither example derives a general physical realization from fusion data.

The open problem explicitly retains the supplier's underlying finite semisimple 2-category, adjoint, and splitting conventions while replacing only its Gray-monoid tensor convention with stated weak tensor data. It retains the absence of automatic unitarity or physical realization and does not present the classification question as proved.
